categories.numbers: Samuel & Kings vs Chronicles — parallel accounts with different numbers
categories.history: Old Testament accounts that appear to disagree
categories.gospels: Gospel accounts of the same event that differ
categories.acts: Acts and the rest of the New Testament

items.title: 700 or 7,000 charioteers; horsemen or footmen?

passages.says: 700 chariots and 40,000 horsemen; Shobach killed
7,000 men who fought in chariots and 40,000 footmen; Shophach killed

explanations: Copying error in a number (Hebrew numbers were easily confused)
Different units counted (chariots vs. chariot crews)

items.title: 700 or 7,000 horsemen captured

passages.says: 1,000 chariots, 700 horsemen, 20,000 footmen
1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, 20,000 footmen

explanations: Copying error in Samuel's Hebrew text
items.note: The Septuagint of 2 Samuel 8:4 and the Samuel scroll from Qumran (4QSamᵃ) read 1,000 chariots and 7,000 horsemen, like Chronicles.

items.title: David's census totals

passages.says: Israel 800,000; Judah 500,000

explanations: Different groups counted (e.g. standing army included or not)
1 Chr 21:6 says Levi and Benjamin were not counted
Copying errors

items.title: Who moved David to take the census — God or Satan?

passages.says: The LORD's anger was kindled, and "he moved David" to number Israel
"Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David" to number Israel

explanations: God permitted what Satan carried out (compare Job 1–2)
Chronicles reflects a later theology that attributes the temptation to an adversary
items.note: The Hebrew in Chronicles is śāṭān without the article, which some read as "an adversary."

items.title: Seven or three years of famine

passages.says: "seven years of famine"
"three years' famine"

explanations: Copying error in Samuel's Hebrew text
Seven counts the three-year famine of 2 Sam 21:1 plus the census year and three more
items.note: The Septuagint of 2 Samuel 24:13 reads three years, like Chronicles.

items.title: 50 shekels of silver or 600 shekels of gold

passages.says: David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for 50 shekels of silver
David gave for "the place" 600 shekels of gold

explanations: Samuel prices the floor and oxen; Chronicles prices the whole site (later the temple mount)

items.title: Solomon's horse stalls: 40,000 or 4,000

passages.says: 40,000 stalls of horses
4,000 stalls for horses and chariots

explanations: Copying error in Kings (the parallel 1 Kgs 10:26 has 1,400 chariots)

items.title: The bronze Sea held 2,000 or 3,000 baths

passages.says: "it contained two thousand baths"
"it received and held three thousand baths"

explanations: Normal contents vs. full capacity
Copying error

items.title: 3,300 or 3,600 overseers

passages.says: 3,300 officers over the work
3,600 to oversee them

explanations: Different ranks counted (2 Chr 8:10 and 1 Kgs 9:23 give 250 and 550 chief officers; both totals come to 3,850)

items.title: 420 or 450 talents of gold from Ophir

passages.says: 420 talents
450 talents

explanations: Gross vs. net (expenses deducted)
Copying error

items.title: Ahaziah began to reign at 22 or 42

passages.says: "Two and twenty years old"
"Forty and two years old" (KJV, following the Hebrew)

explanations: Copying error in Chronicles: his father Jehoram died at 40 (2 Chr 21:20), so 42 would make Ahaziah older than his father
items.note: Some Septuagint manuscripts and the Syriac read 20 or 22 in 2 Chronicles 22:2; most modern translations print 22.

items.title: Jehoiachin began to reign at 18 or 8

passages.says: "eighteen years old… reigned three months"
"eight years old… reigned three months and ten days"

explanations: Copying error in Chronicles (Ezek 19:5–7 describes him as a grown man with wives, 2 Kgs 24:15)
Co-regency from age 8
items.note: Some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint and the Syriac read 18 in Chronicles.

items.title: David's chief warrior: 800 or 300 killed

passages.says: Adino the Eznite, against 800, slain at one time
Jashobeam lifted his spear against 300, slain at one time

explanations: Copying error in one of the numbers or names (the Samuel Hebrew is difficult here)
Two different exploits

items.title: Baasha attacks Judah ten years after he died?

passages.says: Baasha's son Elah began to reign in Asa's 26th year (so Baasha was already dead)
"In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah"

explanations: Counted from the division of the kingdom, not from Asa's accession
Copying error in the number

items.title: Was Hezekiah born when his father was 11?

passages.says: Ahaz was 20 when he began and reigned 16 years (died at about 36)
Hezekiah was 25 when he began to reign

explanations: Co-regencies overlapping the reigns
Copying error in one of the ages

items.title: Who killed Goliath — David or Elhanan?

passages.says: David killed the Philistine (Goliath, 17:4)
Elhanan "slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite" — the words "the brother of" are in italics in the KJV: they are not in the Hebrew, which says Elhanan killed Goliath
Elhanan slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath

explanations: Copying error in 2 Samuel; Chronicles preserves the original ("Lahmi" and "Bethlehemite" look similar in Hebrew)
Elhanan was another name for David
Two different giants named Goliath

items.title: How did Saul die?

passages.says: Saul fell on his own sword
An Amalekite says "I stood upon him, and slew him"
"[Saul] enquired not of the LORD: therefore he slew him"

explanations: The Amalekite lied to win David's favor
Chronicles states the theological cause, not the physical means
items.note: See also 1 Sam 28:6: "when Saul enquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not" — compare with 1 Chr 10:14.

items.title: Did Michal have children?

passages.says: Michal "had no child unto the day of her death"
"the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel" (KJV)

explanations: Copying error: Merab, not Michal, married Adriel (1 Sam 18:19)
Michal raised her sister's sons (the KJV's "brought up")
items.note: Two Hebrew manuscripts and some Septuagint manuscripts read Merab in 2 Sam 21:8.

items.title: Animals before or after the man?

passages.says: Animals are made, then humankind, male and female together
The man is formed first; then the LORD forms the animals and brings them to him; the woman last

explanations: Two separate creation accounts from different sources
Genesis 2 is topical, not chronological ("had formed", as in some translations)

items.title: Two of every kind, or seven?

passages.says: two of every sort, male and female
clean beasts by sevens; unclean by two

explanations: Two sources combined
Genesis 6 gives the general rule, Genesis 7 the detail for clean animals

items.title: How Judas died, and who bought the field

passages.says: Judas hanged himself; the chief priests bought the potter's field with the money
Judas "purchased a field"; "falling headlong, he burst asunder"

explanations: He hanged himself and the body later fell
The priests bought it with his money, so it was counted as his purchase

items.title: Who was Joseph's father?

passages.says: Jacob begat Joseph
Joseph, "which was the son of Heli"

explanations: Luke gives Mary's line (Heli as Joseph's father-in-law)
Levirate marriage: one legal, one natural father
The lists also differ between David and Joseph almost entirely

items.title: One blind man or two; leaving or approaching Jericho?

passages.says: Two blind men, as they departed from Jericho
Blind Bartimaeus, as he went out of Jericho
A certain blind man, as he was come nigh unto Jericho

explanations: Mark and Luke name only the better-known man
Old and new Jericho were two sites, so one could leave one and approach the other

items.title: One demoniac or two; where?

passages.says: Two possessed men, in the country of the Gergesenes (KJV)
One man, in the country of the Gadarenes
One man, in the country of the Gadarenes

explanations: Mark and Luke focus on the one who spoke
The place names vary in manuscripts (Gadarenes, Gerasenes, Gergesenes)

items.title: The third hour or the sixth?

passages.says: "it was the third hour, and they crucified him"
Pilate is still judging Jesus "about the sixth hour"

explanations: John uses Roman time (from midnight), Mark Jewish time (from sunrise)
Approximate times by quarters of the day
items.note: A few manuscripts of John read "third hour."

items.title: Was the Last Supper the Passover meal?

passages.says: On the first day of unleavened bread, "when they killed the passover," the disciples prepare the Passover
The next morning the priests avoid defilement "that they might eat the passover"
"it was the preparation of the passover" when Jesus was condemned

explanations: Different calendars in use
"Passover" in John means the whole feast week
John aligns Jesus' death with the slaughter of the lambs for theological reasons

items.title: Take a staff or not?

passages.says: "take nothing for their journey, save a staff only"
"neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves"
"Take nothing for your journey, neither staves"

explanations: Don't acquire an extra staff vs. take the one you have
Different sayings preserved differently

items.title: Before the cock crows once or twice?

passages.says: "before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice"
"before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice"

explanations: Matthew, Luke and John simplify; Mark gives the detail (Mark 14:68, 72)
items.note: Some manuscripts of Mark lack the first crowing and "twice."

items.title: Was Jairus's daughter already dead?

passages.says: "My daughter is even now dead"
"My little daughter lieth at the point of death"; news of her death comes later (5:35)

explanations: Matthew condenses the story, combining the request and the later news

items.title: Who went to the tomb, and whom did they see?

passages.says: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary; one angel sitting on the stone
Two Marys and Salome; a young man sitting inside
The women (named in 24:10: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary mother of James, others); two men standing
Mary Magdalene (then two angels sitting, 20:12)

explanations: Each writer names part of a larger group and different moments
Independent eyewitness traditions differ in detail

items.title: The wording on the cross

passages.says: THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS
THE KING OF THE JEWS
THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS
JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS

explanations: The sign was in three languages (John 19:20), so wording may differ
Each gives the substance

items.title: Did both thieves mock Jesus?

passages.says: "The thieves also, which were crucified with him, cast the same in his teeth"
One railed on him; the other rebuked him

explanations: Both mocked at first, then one repented
Matthew uses a general plural

items.title: Did Paul's companions hear the voice?

passages.says: "hearing a voice, but seeing no man"
"saw indeed the light… but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me"

explanations: They heard a sound but did not understand the words (the Greek grammar differs between the two verses)
items.note: Acts 26:14 adds that they all fell to the ground; Acts 9:7 says they stood.

items.title: Does God tempt anyone?

passages.says: "God did tempt Abraham" (KJV)
"God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man"

explanations: The Hebrew nissah means 'test'; most modern translations read 'God tested Abraham'
James means enticing to sin, not testing faith

items.title: Does God change his mind?

passages.says: "it repented the LORD that he had made man"
"the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do"
"God is not a man… that he should repent"
"the Strength of Israel will not… repent" — eleven verses after 15:11 says he did

explanations: Human language for God's response to changed circumstances (anthropopathism)
God's character and promises don't change, his responses to people do
items.note: 1 Samuel 15:11 and 15:29 sit in the same chapter, so the writer saw no conflict.

items.title: Has anyone seen God?

passages.says: Jacob: "I have seen God face to face"
"the LORD spake unto Moses face to face"
"Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live"
"No man hath seen God at any time"

explanations: 'Face to face' is an idiom for direct, personal encounter
People saw a manifestation (an angel, glory, the pre-incarnate Son), not God's essence

items.title: Justified by faith or by works?

passages.says: "a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law"
"a man is not justified by the works of the law"
"by works a man is justified, and not by faith only"

explanations: Paul means works of the Mosaic law as a basis for standing with God; James means deeds that show faith is real
Luther thought the conflict real and called James 'an epistle of straw'

items.title: Are children punished for their parents' sins?

passages.says: "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation"
"the children [shall not] be put to death for the fathers"
"The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father"

explanations: Exodus describes consequences that follow families who keep hating God; Deuteronomy is a rule for human courts
Ezekiel answers a proverb (18:2) and marks a development in teaching

items.title: Honour or hate your father and mother?

passages.says: "Honour thy father and thy mother"
"If any man… hate not his father, and mother… he cannot be my disciple"

explanations: A Semitic idiom: 'hate' means 'love less' (compare Matt 10:37; Gen 29:30–31)

items.title: Peace or a sword?

passages.says: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you"
"on earth peace, good will toward men"
"I came not to send peace, but a sword"

explanations: Inner peace with God vs. the division his message causes in families (Matt 10:35–36)

items.title: Judge or don't judge?

passages.says: "Judge not, that ye be not judged"
"Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment"
"the saints shall judge the world"

explanations: Condemning hypocritically vs. discerning rightly (Matt 7:5 assumes you will help your brother)

items.title: Answer a fool or not?

passages.says: "Answer not a fool according to his folly"
"Answer a fool according to his folly"

explanations: Placed side by side deliberately: wisdom means knowing which situation calls for which

items.title: Bear one another's burdens or your own?

passages.says: "Bear ye one another's burdens"
"every man shall bear his own burden"

explanations: Different Greek words: baros (heavy weight, v. 2) and phortion (one's own pack or responsibility, v. 5)

items.title: Does God get tired?

passages.says: "on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed"
"the Creator… fainteth not, neither is weary"

explanations: 'Rested' (shabath) means ceased; 'refreshed' is human language
Different genres: law grounded in a creation pattern vs. poetry about God's power

items.title: Has anyone gone up to heaven?

passages.says: "Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven"
"Enoch… was not; for God took him"
"no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven"

explanations: John means no one has gone up to bring back heavenly knowledge
'Heaven' in 2 Kings may mean the sky

items.title: Swear oaths or not?

passages.says: "Thou shalt fear the LORD… and shalt swear by his name"
A vow or oath must be kept
"Swear not at all"
"swear not… let your yea be yea"

explanations: Jesus targets evasive oaths (Matt 5:35–37; 23:16–22), not all solemn statements; Paul uses oath-like language (Gal 1:20)
Some traditions (Quakers, Anabaptists) take it literally

items.title: Is Jesus' witness about himself true?

passages.says: "If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true"
"Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true"

explanations: John 5 concedes the legal rule (two witnesses, Deut 19:15) for argument's sake; John 8 asserts his authority

items.title: Is the Law forever or abolished?

passages.says: "I am not come to destroy the law… till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass"
"Having abolished in his flesh… the law of commandments"
The first covenant is "ready to vanish away"

explanations: Fulfilled rather than discarded; ceremonial vs. moral law distinctions
Jewish readers see the Torah as eternal (e.g. Exod 31:16 'a perpetual covenant')

items.title: Is divorce allowed?

passages.says: A man may write a bill of divorcement
Whoever divorces and remarries commits adultery — no exception
"except it be for fornication"

explanations: Jesus says Moses permitted divorce 'because of the hardness of your hearts' (Matt 19:8)
Matthew's exception clause is read by many as clarifying Mark
